headline: El debate por la unión civil
content: The Commission of Justice of Congress will discuss the topic after Easter Week. Minister Omonte asked for tolerance and respect towards minorities.  The Commission of justice of Congress, chaired by Juan Carlos Eguren, estimated initially that it would deliberate over the proposed laws regarding civil union among homosexuals presented during April but now expects to start discussions early May.  In front of such situation, the minister of Womens Affairs, Carmen Omonte, requested respect toward minorities and defended discussion within Congress. One should have enough tolerance to look upon the needs of society collectively while respecting its minority groups.

headline: Carlos Ramos Heredia, nuevo fiscal de la Nación
content: Magistrate Carlos Ramos Heredia was designated yesterday as the new Attorney General replacing José Antonio Pérez starting next May for three years. Immediately concerns arose about his alleged connections to corruption cases involving narcotic trafficking.   It’s regrettable that someone has been chosen despite these issues, said congressman Martin Belaúnde (SP).  Juan Carlos Eguren (PPC) demanded that Mr. Ramos clarify soon any questions related to those allegations. Meanwhile, Ganá Peru supported his designation.

headline: No tengo impedimentos tcnicos ni jurdicos, y ninguna llamada de atención en 33 aos d e trayectoria.
content: Carlos Ramos Heredia, newly appointed Fiscal of the Nation stated there were neither technical nor legal obstacles against him having had a career spanning thirty-three years free of warnings.

headline: Operacion Perseo
content: Policemen arrested last night twenty-six individuals linked to Movadef following six months operation aimed at uncovering funding sources behind this pro-Sendero organization. Among those detained include Alfredo Crespo and Manuel Farjad attorneys representing Abimael Guzmán and former President Humalas cousin, Walter Humala. They face charges including affiliation with terrorism and money laundering.

headline: Menos rezo, mas lectura
content: The worst form of hypocrisy I encounter involves conceding support for civil unions yet opposing marriage rights and adoption by homosexual couples. Personally, I find hypocrites who justify their stance using Bible verses more bearable than outright bigots whose ignorance fuels fanaticism. Their lack of intellectual depth embarrassingly highlights how some people refuse even to question their beliefs under faiths guise.  Despite widespread acceptance of religious psychosis, we reason-driven folks struggle to make headway. Those carrying religion like banners often overlook Gods terrifying nature depicted in the Old Testament—a character described vividly by Richard Dawkins in *The Selfish Gene*. Yet many believers reinterpret divine teachings focusing solely on love and goodness inherent in humanity. While differing fundamentally from my belief system, I still hold deep respect for their intentions which seem rooted in kindness and inclusivity.  However, rational discourse finds little room here. In The Righteous Mind, psychologist Jonathan Haidt suggests our reasoning serves emotional instincts rather than guiding principles. Our initial reactions shape subsequent arguments supporting what feels morally right—an insight suggesting emotions drive morality leading to conflicts fueled by inherited biases shaped through natural selection. Despite seeming predetermined paths, science offers hope via environmental influences softening rigid stances alongside state-enforced equal protection ensuring fair treatment across societal spectrums regardless of individual differences.

headline: EL PERÚ CRECE 5,5 % ESTE AÑO
content: The World Bank aligns with IMF estimates predicting a 5.5 percent growth rate for Perus economy marking second-highest expansion in Latin America trailing Panamas seven percent increase. This projection underscores significant economic momentum amidst regional developments.

headline: BCP Renueva su Identidad Visual
content: On celebrating its 125th anniversary, Banco de Crdito del Per unveiled a refreshed brand identity featuring a redesigned logo symbolizing modernity, closeness, and dynamism. Alongside physical updates visible across branches nationwide, digital enhancements aim to improve user experience online reflecting commitment to customer-centric service delivery.

headline: Avion solar vuela 120 horas sin parar
content: The solar-powered aircraft, Solar Impulse 2 aims to circumnavigate Earth come spring 2015 demonstrated endurance flying beyond 120 hours non-stop covering five days and nights essential for ocean crossings. Measuring approximately seventy-two meters akin to an Airbus A380 albeit weighing significantly less showcases technological advancements enabling sustainable aviation solutions.

headline: Certamen Internacional de Badminton Inaugura Hoy
content: Ayer comenzó en el Coliseo Manuel Bonilla de Miraflores el XIX Campeonato Internacional de Badminton. Participación de 24 países de América, Europa y Asia, con un total de 121 deportistas.

headline: Triunfos Destacados en Competición de Badminton
content: Resalto la victoria de la dupla mixta nacional conformada por Mario Cuba y Katherine Winder contra los argentinos Lucio Coronato y Florencia Bernardine por 21–8 y 21–7. Además, Martín Del Valle superó al portugués Hugo Vasconsuelos por 16–21, 21–19 y 21–15.

content: Anoche, en el Colegio Salesiano de Breña, Sporting Cristal derrotó al Deportivo Wanka 25–16, 25–15 y 25–23 en partidos de ida por los cuartos de final de la Liga Nacional Superior de Voley. Resaltar actuación destacada de Maguilaura Franco.

content: Continúa competiendo Felipe Ros después de suspensión inicial por condiciones climáticas severas. Logró sexto lugar en tercer etapa desde Zapala, Neuquén. También destaca participación de Eduardo Heinrich posicionándose undécimo.

headline: POR QU SE DEBEN RECICLAR LOS DISPOSITIVOS ELECTRONICOS?
content: Botar estos aparatos en cualquier lado tiene un costo ambiental muy alto, pues contienen materiales como el plomo y el mercurio, muy daninos para la naturaleza y nuestra salud. Mucho antes las tiendas especializadas deberán tener puntos de acopio gratis.   Para su fabricación, las empresas utilizan muchos elementos peligrosos como mercurio, cobre y plomo, le explica a Publimetro Raúl Roca, especialista del Ministerio del Ambiente (MINAM). Los efectos de estos metales pesados no se crecen a la naturaleza. También tienen consecuencias directas para la salud de las personas, acota Roca. Pone como ejemplo una práctica muy extendida. Cuando la gente quema cables viejos para aprovechar el cobre que contienen, están inhalando gases muy nocivos para su propia salud, dice.   Por eso, lo ideal es no desechar de estos dispositivos en cualquier sitio cuando acaben su vida útil. Deben ir a un vertedero seguro donde se encapsulen para no liberar nada dañino al medio ambiente, comenta Roca. Solamente algunas municipalidades organizan campañas por propia iniciativa o en conjunto con otras entidades para acopiar los aparatos eléctricos y electrónicos. Algunos distritos tienen sus propias campañas de reciclaje de estos residuos. Alianzas estratégicas con asociaciones para que los ayuden a tratar adecuadamente estos residuos. En otras campañas de Surco, durante el mes de DICIEMBRE solamente el 15% de los vecinos realizan una participación. Campaña de acopio en el Parque de la Amistad, SI EL VECINO LO SOLICITA, PERSONAL DEL MUNICIPIO PODRIA IR A RECOGER LOS APARATOS VIEJOS A SU DOMICILIO.
